conclusion: No counterexample construction with |A| exponential in |S| exists in any lane I could develop, and the tensor lane is now closed conditionally: every mixed pair of a tensor A.B is a solution of the S-unit equation x+y=1, so an exponential tensor would force exponentially many S-unit solutions, beating the best known construction there. The two findings that travel further are corrections to the parent: the refutation bar is a bounded-prime-cost doubling rather than a full composition law, and an anti-composition theorem is not sufficient for #126.
confidence: The five theorems in RESULTS.md are short and self-contained; Lemma 1, Lemma 2, Prop 3, Prop 4 and the tensor identity are checkable in a minute each and I would let someone lean on them fully. Theorem 5 and Corollary 5.1 I would lean on for the tensor lane only, and the conditional half rests on the standard expectation that S-unit solution counts are subexponential, which is open - do not report the lane as closed unconditionally. The measured table is a bounded-box lower bound and nothing more; rows 1-7 agreeing with the parent from an independent solver is real corroboration, rows 8 and 9 are new lower bounds only. Lemma 2 is elementary enough that it is probably in the literature; I did not search.
